post.summary: Open a checkout for a quote
post.description:
Resolves the browser Origin as /v1/public/trips does. Takes a quote by id and charges its stored total, never an amount the client sends. The quote must be this operator's, unused, and still valid by the database clock; the guest must have accepted its policy version. Holds the quote's party on the trip, which checks the party against the product and the seats left, holds included; writes the immutable order copied from the quote and a pending payment on the operator's connected account; then creates the provider payment and returns what the guest needs to pay.

The guest's client generates `checkoutSecret` and keeps it; TideGrid stores only its hash. Idempotent by key: a retry with the same key and body returns the same checkout with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and creates the provider payment if an earlier attempt could not; the same key with another body answers 422. A 503 `payment_provider_unavailable` means the checkout exists and the provider did not answer: retry the same request.

Rate limited per client address and operator like quotes, and at most 3 open checkouts per client address at a time. A limited request answers 429 and writes nothing.

get.summary: What the guest needs to pay an open checkout, read again
get.description:
Resolves the browser Origin as /v1/public/trips does and needs the checkout's secret as a bearer token, never a URL. For an open checkout within its expiry, returns the provider payment and its client secret, so a page that reloaded, or lost the answer to opening the checkout, can still pay without sending the booker's details again. It asks the provider with the payment's own idempotency key, so it never creates a second payment, and reads the checkout again once the provider answers. Any other state answers 200 with `payment: null`, whether or not payments are configured, including a checkout that closes or lapses while it is read, while the provider answers, or while the card form's account is read: the body then shows the closed state. A wrong secret, another operator's checkout, and an unknown id answer the same 404, whether or not payments are configured.

Never cached. Rate limited like public commands, since it may call the provider. The client secret is a capability: keep it out of URLs and logs.

Under the Stripe provider the payment also carries `stripe`: the platform's test-mode publishable key and the connected account the payment was created on, which Stripe.js needs to mount the card-only Payment Element. Only this read returns them. Without a valid test-mode publishable key in local, preview, or staging, an open checkout answers 503 `payments_unavailable` before the provider is asked.

post.summary: Receive a signed payment provider event
post.description: For the payment provider only. The body is the provider's event, signed over its raw bytes with a timestamp (the fake provider's `Fake-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`; Stripe's `Stripe-Signature` in the same scheme, when the Stripe adapter is configured, which no deployment does yet). A signature outside the tolerance window, or for another body, answers 400 and nothing is recorded. A Stripe event must be a snapshot Connect event in test mode; a live, platform-scope, or thin event answers 400 payload_invalid. A verified event is recorded once per event id; a duplicate changes nothing, and a Stripe redelivery whose per-delivery fields changed counts as the same event. A booking is confirmed only here or by the sweep, from a verified event. A 500 leaves the event recorded and unprocessed for the provider's retry and the sweep. Under Stripe only: the client address (`CF-Connecting-IP`) must be one of Stripe's published webhook addresses, or the route answers 403 source_not_allowed before reading the body; and a newly recorded event answers 200 with outcome `received` before it is processed, after the response, with the sweep as the backstop.

post.summary: Book a guest at no charge, as an owner
post.description:
Owners only (bookings.create and the owner role; anyone else answers 403 complimentary_forbidden). Takes a quote this tenant's staff created, as a staff checkout does, and in one step holds the party, writes the order, records the owner's grant for the order's whole total with a reason code (a note is required for other), and confirms the booking. There is no payment, and the booking's source is complimentary. Never on a trip that takes a deposit (409 complimentary_deposit). An owner may add a capacityOverride as on a staff checkout.

The booking is otherwise a booking like any other: the confirmation email with the management link and waiver requests goes to the booker, and it can be moved, made smaller, or canceled. Canceling it returns nothing, since nothing was paid. TideGrid charges no fee on it.

Staff attest as for a staff checkout. Idempotent by key: a retry with the same key and body returns the same booking with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Send a booking's email again
post.description:
Owners and booking staff. Sends the booking's confirmation (with a new management link) or its cancellation notice again, as a new message, to the booker's address on file, rendered from the booking as it is now. The new link is minted when the email is sent; earlier links are superseded then, and still renew. An earlier email of the same kind still waiting to go out is canceled (code resent). The reason code is recorded in the audit history. Never a retry of an earlier message: delivery sends each message at most once.

Limits, for every staff member and request: at most 5 sends again per booking that were attempted or are still waiting, at least 10 minutes after the booking's last one, and 50 an hour per operator. Idempotent by key: a refusal is the key's stored answer and replays as the same 409; send again with a new key.

Order: authentication (401), membership (404), permission (403), the key's replay, the booking (404), then booking_email_off (409) when this environment sends no email, which stores nothing for the key.

A request whose work ran longer than the database allows a resend (30 s, as when it waited behind other resends) answers 503 booking_email_busy: nothing was sent or stored, so the same request may be sent again with the same key.
